authoredFrom: PS5/PS6 — a RESERVED WORD IS NOT A CALL, and nothing is emitted from a recovery region. Authored 2026-09-26. TWO of the classes here are invisible to every gate this repository has. (a) NAMED BLOCKS: the grammar models `Begin`/`Process`/`End` as `command` nodes — reproduced in isolation as `hasError=false`, `command nodes: ["End","Process","Begin"]` — and the pre-wave `FLOW_KEYWORDS` did not list them, so every advanced function emitted three fabricated `calls` edges naming its own block keywords; hand-confirmed at `dsc/pwsh.profile.resource.ps1:15-16` of the pinned corpus. (b) `if` AS AN EXPRESSION: `$mode = if (…) { } elseif (…) { } else { }` parses with `hasError = FALSE` and still leaves `elseif`/`else` as bare `command` nodes — F1 cannot see it (the node type is real), F10 cannot see it (the file is not damaged) and the M12 corpus-errors census cannot see it (it counts ERROR nodes). That is why `script/m60/powershell-keyword-census.ts` exists. (c) DSC: before the fix, 4 of 4 relationships in a representative configuration were fabrications (`Configuration`, `node`, `File`, `Destination`).

expectComplexity.comment: PS13: a `switch` CASE is a decision point. The pre-wave `isBranch` list named `switch_statement` but not `switch_clause`, so this file's three-case switch contributed 1 instead of 3 and the pre-fix figure was 1. Verified in isolation: a four-clause switch measures 6 (1 base + 1 statement + 4 clauses). `metadata.complexity` is NOT this and must not be substituted — it is symbols + relationships, so it grows with the analyzer's own output and pinning it would pin the regression in place.
